items.stem: The price of coffee rises. What usually happens to the quantity of coffee demanded?
items.objective: apply the law of demand as a movement along the curve

items.stem: A new technology cuts the cost of producing laptops. What happens in the laptop market?
items.objective: predict the effect of a supply shift on equilibrium price

items.stem: A price rises by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 20%. What is the absolute value of the price elasticity of demand?
items.objective: compute price elasticity of demand from percentage changes

items.stem: The government sets a binding price ceiling below equilibrium. What is the result?
items.objective: predict the effect of a binding price ceiling

items.stem: You skip a $20 concert to work a shift that pays $50. What is the opportunity cost of working?
items.objective: identify opportunity cost as the next best alternative forgone

items.stem: Which would shift the demand curve for electric cars to the right? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The price of electric cars falls
A tax credit for buying electric cars
Consumer incomes rise, if electric cars are a normal good

items.objective: distinguish demand shifters from a change in the good's own price
